chapter: Chords, recordings and his own groups
title: The Prestige date he suggested Hawkins for; the leader's name switched
summary: He hired Hawkins, but on reissue Hawkins's name replaced his as leader, and the producers chose the sidemen.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: ... Well when I got the date -- See the only thing was wrong with them a couple of times -- not a couple of times, but every time -- they would select the musicians. And there I'm playing with a strange group of guys -- not that they can't play -- but they haven't played together, you've got to get acquainted. You could be the best baseball player in the world but shit, you still got to know each other...

The thing of it is when we made this record date with Prestige, with Coleman Hawkins -- when they offered me the date I say I think I can get Coleman Hawkins. Well they jump straight up, like "you can!" I say yeah. And I asked him we were good friends, he said "yeah" ... get a date, sure." So we got this date and played this thing, I think it was one of 'em called Marching Along. It was a long, it was too long for me and I wasn't prepared for the damn thing, I ain't sure -- Marchin' Along I believe ... He was on it and Ray Bryant was on it ...
But the thing of it is, after the first date, and the record sold good, then I think we had another one. I know I had another date at Prestige. ...
Now after this date ... I know anyhow they
reissued the thing and put Coleman Hawkins 364. name [as leader].
